cards.text: Job has been getting question after question from the LORD, and he just put his hand over his mouth. He's got nothing to add. But the LORD isn't done, and He answers Job again out of the whirlwind.

cards.question: Job's gone quiet, so the LORD tells him he can stop answering now.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me." Friend, "brace yourself" has never ONCE been followed by "here, have a cookie."

cards.question: The LORD asks Job if he would really annul His justice. Would Job condemn God to ___ himself?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like His?" Friend, my arms are a MUSTACHE, and the loudest voice in my old kitchen was Mags.
Then the LORD hands Job a challenge: clothe yourself with honor and glory, and unleash the fury of your wrath. That's like getting handed the keys to the whole bakery and told, okay, YOU run it.

cards.question: In the LORD's challenge, what is Job told to do to every proud man?

answers.text: Look on him and bring him low
Pray for him and let him go
Warn him and give him time

cards.question: Humble the proud, trample the wicked, bury them in the dust. If Job could pull all that off, what does the LORD say He would confess?

answers.text: That Job's own right hand can save him
That Job was right all along
That Job should rule the nations

cards.text: Then the LORD points Job to a creature: "Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you." Same Maker, friend. VERY different workout plan.

cards.question: The LORD says Behemoth feeds on ___ like an ox.

cards.text: And this grass-eater is BUILT: a tail that sways like a cedar, bones that are tubes of bronze, limbs that are rods of iron. Meanwhile I'm a stamper with a mustache, feeling real underdressed.

cards.question: The LORD calls Behemoth the foremost of His works. Who is the only one who can draw the sword against him?

cards.text: So where does a creature this big hang out? Under the lotus plants, hidden in the reeds of the marsh, like me napping in the shade after a big batch.

cards.question: While Behemoth rests by the marsh, the beasts of the field run and hide from him.

cards.text: But what if the river rages? What if the Jordan surges right up to his mouth?

cards.question: Even when the river rages, Behemoth stays unafraid and secure.
The LORD finishes with Behemoth on one last question. What does it ask?

cards.text: Pierce his nose with a snare while he WATCHES you? Friend, I spent a whole morning chasing one sprinkle under the oven and never caught it.
Then the LORD turns to another creature, Leviathan: "Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?"

cards.question: The LORD keeps the questions coming about Leviathan. What are they all asking Job?

answers.text: Whether Job could tame and control him
Whether Job has ever seen him up close
Whether Job knows where he lives

cards.text: "Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?" Friend, I'm stuck on a GOLD BASE, so if I put Leviathan on a leash, he's walking ME.

cards.question: The LORD says if Job lays a hand on Leviathan, he'll remember the ___ and never repeat it.

cards.text: Hope of overcoming him? False. Just the sight of him is overwhelming, and no one is fierce enough to rouse him.

cards.question: Nobody dares stir up Leviathan. Then the LORD turns the point toward Himself. What does He ask?

answers.text: Who is able to stand against Me
Who is brave enough to hunt him
Who will warn the people of the sea

cards.question: The LORD says He has to repay people for what they've given Him.

cards.text: "Everything under heaven is Mine." Friend, the expired coupon in my old junk drawer STILL thinks somebody owes it something.
Then the LORD says He can't keep silent about Leviathan's body. His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.

cards.question: How tightly are Leviathan's scales joined?

answers.text: So tight no air can pass between them
Loose enough for water to slip through
Spread apart like feathers on a wing

cards.text: And then it gets WILD. His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.

cards.question: Fire and smoke come out of Leviathan, with flames from his mouth and smoke from his nostrils.

cards.text: His breath sets coals ablaze. Friend, I've spent YEARS preheating ovens, and this guy does it just by BREATHING.
Strength resides in his neck, his chest is as hard as a rock, and when he rises up, even the mighty are terrified.

cards.question: Swords and spears do nothing to Leviathan, but an arrow can make him flee.

cards.text: He regards iron as straw, and he LAUGHS at the sound of the lance. Friend, somebody drops one cookie tray near me and I jump a foot in the air, gold base and all.

cards.question: Leviathan leaves a glistening wake, and one would think the deep had white hair. How does the LORD sum him up?

answers.text: Nothing on earth is his equal
He is the oldest of all creatures
He is afraid only of the deep

cards.question: Leviathan looks down on all the haughty. He is king over all the ___.

cards.text: Then Job replies to the LORD. Friend, after hearing about a creature whose breath sets coals ablaze, I'd need a minute too.

cards.question: Job starts with what he now knows. What is it?

answers.text: That God can do all things

cards.question: Job admits he spoke about things he did not understand, things too wonderful for him to know.

cards.text: Then Job quotes the LORD back: "I will question you, and you shall inform Me." That line again, from the start of this whole speech.

cards.question: So what's different for Job now?

answers.text: Before he'd heard of God but now he's seen Him
Before he trusted friends but now he trusts himself
Before he was angry but now he is calm

cards.question: Job's last words here: "Therefore I despise myself, and I ___ in dust and ashes."

cards.text: And that's where we leave Job for now, in dust and ashes. Hang tight, friend. This story's got one more page.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 6 quotes "Therefore I despise myself, and I ___ in dust and ashes.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The statement links Job 40:20 to Behemoth resting by the marsh with 'While Behemoth rests by the marsh.' Job 40:20 says 'The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.' It never ties that to his resting in the marsh, which comes in 40:21-22. The card also asks about 40:20 after card 13 has already moved on to 40:21-22. Reword the statement so it doesn't add the link, and place the card before card 13.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup says 'Then the LORD turns the point toward Himself.' Only the right answer, 'Who is able to stand against Me,' points to God. The two wrong answers are about Leviathan and the sea, so the setup rules them out and gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 9 already says the scales are 'tightly sealed together.' That rules out both wrong answers, 'Loose enough for water to slip through' and 'Spread apart like feathers on a wing,' so the question answers itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens with the LORD's first-person words, 'Everything under heaven is Mine.' The card itself never says who is speaking.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: 'So what's different for Job now?' leans on cards that are no longer on screen. It doesn't say what has changed or what it is compared with, such as how Job knew God before and how he knows Him now (Job 42:5).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
